record.name: Nepal
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. The National AI Policy 2025 gives the AI Regulation Council compliance duties and the National AI Centre standards, programme evaluation and risk-management functions. These provisions do not establish evaluation of advanced models for capabilities or behaviour risks.

check.language_note: The recorded ne queries use a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. English queries were also run on 17 October 2026; the previously recorded national or official-language coverage and its limits are unchanged. The additional status review used Nepali and English queries and both policy versions; decisive Nepali clauses were checked visually because extraction has font-mapping errors. Search batches for the additional status review, using 1-based positions in check.searches: 3, 4; 5, 6, 7. Each group records the same exact registered URLs found in its combined search results, without attribution to an individual query. Explicit page opens and finds and unverified URL variants are excluded. Groups list the recorded queries; some requests also contained additional queries retained in the research evidence.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: The Techpana page was blocked and even its title was not verified. Confidence was low under that rule; none_identified is a bounded search finding, not proof of absence.
check.governance_note: The Nepali original and English ministry policy specify Council compliance and Centre coordination, standards and programme evaluation. Neither establishes the qualifying remit to test advanced models. Both search languages were used, supporting medium confidence for this bounded negative.

related_bodies.name: AI Regulation Council
related_bodies.role: Its Nepali compliance clause requires adherence to approved AI policies, laws and standards. The English version also says to test compliance. It is a minister-chaired Council under policy section 10.1. The Rising Nepal reported on 10 November 2025 that the minister said the Council had formed. No constituting decision was retrieved.

related_bodies.name: National AI Centre
related_bodies.role: Policy section 10.2 assigns it programme evaluation, product and service standards, risk mitigation and the Council secretariat. It is a centre under the communications ministry, reported by The Rising Nepal as inaugurated on 10 November 2025. These tasks do not establish evaluation of advanced models for capabilities or behaviour risks.

related_bodies.name: AI Excellence Centres
related_bodies.role: They are planned in universities and research institutions for AI research and training.

record.notes: The Nepali and English ministry policies distinguish the Council's compliance role in section 10.1.1(d) from the Centre's standards, programme evaluation and risk-management functions in section 10.2.1. The Nepali clause says to ensure compliance with approved policies, laws and standards; the English version adds testing. Neither wording establishes general-purpose or frontier-model capability or behaviour-risk evaluation. Policy actions 9.5 and 9.10 concern benchmarking, standardisation, certification and a regulatory sandbox. Section 14 addresses risks to policy implementation, rather than a model-testing mandate. The earlier review flag incorrectly attributed the Council's compliance clause to the Centre. The Rising Nepal reports the Centre's inauguration on 10 November 2025 and the minister's statement that the Council had formed; no constituting decision was retrieved. Nepali and English searches found no later official extension to a qualifying remit to evaluate advanced models.

next_check.reason: Seek constituting decisions and any later testing rules for the AI Regulation Council and National AI Centre; reassess if either receives a technical remit to evaluate advanced models for capabilities or behaviour risks.
